steps.title: The browser on either side, and closed in one click
steps.body: The browser drawer can open on the left, next to your projects, instead of the right: choose it in the drawer's menu. While it is open, the Browser button in the project bar steps aside; the X beside the hide arrow closes the browser, every tab of the project, at once. Hidden with pages still open, the Browser button keeps a dot.

keys.text: in the drawer's menu (and back on the right)

steps.title: Cru uses the browser as fully as a chat
steps.body: Ask Cru to press a button by its name ("Add to Shopping List"), click a spot, drag, pick from a list, fill a form, read the console or the page's requests. It looks in an open dialog first, tells you what it actually clicked, and sees what on a page can be clicked.
